title: Junior Data Analyst
summary: An entry-level analyst role in any sector: pulling data from databases, cleaning it, finding what it says and explaining it to people who make decisions. Employers look for SQL, a little Python, clear writing and sound judgement about data.

areas.label: Data analytics
areas.why: The core of the job: asking a question of the data, checking it and reading the result honestly.

areas.label: Where data lives
areas.why: Know the kinds of data store you will meet and how data moves between them.

areas.label: SQL
areas.why: Almost every analyst interview and task asks you to query a database.

areas.label: Python for analysis
areas.why: Clean, reshape and chart data that is too big or too messy for a spreadsheet.

areas.label: Handling data responsibly
areas.why: Personal and confidential data comes with rules. Knowing them early keeps you and your employer safe.

areas.label: Explaining findings
areas.why: An answer nobody understands changes nothing. Practise short, plain write-ups and presenting to non-specialists.

stages.label: Get the foundations
stages.blurb: Understand how analysis works and where data comes from.

stages.label: Build your tools
stages.blurb: Get fluent in SQL and Python on real, messy data.

stages.label: Work responsibly and explain it
stages.blurb: Handle data safely and turn results into something people act on.

stages.label: Show your work
stages.blurb: Put a portfolio together and prepare for interviews.

actions.label: Finish one small analysis project from start to end
actions.detail: Pick a public dataset that interests you. Ask one clear question, clean the data, answer it and write one page on what you found and what you are unsure of.

actions.label: Put two projects somewhere an employer can see them
actions.detail: A public repository or a simple page, each with a short README: the question, the data, the method and the answer.

actions.label: Rewrite your CV around what you have analysed
actions.detail: For each item say the question, the tool you used and the result, with a number where you can.

actions.label: Practise a technical interview out loud
actions.detail: Have a friend set you two SQL questions and ask you to explain a result as if to a manager. Check you can say the answer in two sentences.

apply.label: Apply for roles
apply.detail: Apply to roles that fit as they appear: aim for at least one good application a week. Keep a list of what you sent and its stage, and ask for feedback after every result. You can start before the date above once your portfolio has two projects.
